market_context: United States/general English; home storage of fresh raw fish at 40°F/4°C or below
title: How long does fresh fish last in the refrigerator?

seo.title: How long fresh fish lasts in the fridge and how to store it
seo.meta_description: Fresh raw fish should be cooked or frozen within 1–2 days when held at 40°F (4°C) or below. Keep it cold, covered and separate from ready-to-eat foods.
seo.search_intent: Know how many days fresh fish can stay refrigerated and how to store it safely.

excerpt: Fresh fish is highly perishable. USDA recommends keeping raw fish and shellfish at 40°F (4°C) or below for only 1–2 days before cooking or freezing. FDA similarly says seafood that will be used within two days should be kept on ice or in a clean refrigerator at 40°F or below; otherwise, freeze it.
content_html:
Fresh fish has a shorter refrigerator window than many whole cuts of meat. As a home-storage rule, raw fish and shellfish should be cooked or frozen within 1–2 days when held at 40°F (4°C) or below.

The official window is short

USDA lists 1–2 refrigerated days for raw fish and shellfish before cooking or freezing. FDA gives similar guidance: if seafood will be used within two days, keep it in a clean refrigerator at 40°F or below; otherwise, freeze it.

Why only one or two days?

Fish has delicate tissue, high moisture and microorganisms that can continue changing the food even at refrigeration temperatures. Cold slows deterioration but does not stop it.

How to store it well

Keep fish in the coldest practical part of the refrigerator, covered or sealed to prevent cross-contamination and drying. Whole fish purchased on ice can be kept very cold with clean ice and good drainage rather than sitting in meltwater.

The purchase day matters

The 1–2 day guidance describes home storage, but the earlier supply-chain history still matters. Fish does not become newly fresh when it reaches your refrigerator. Buy seafood that is refrigerated or displayed on a thick bed of fresh ice.

Signs not to wait for the deadline

FDA says fresh fish should smell mild, not sour, rancid or ammonia-like, and the flesh should be firm. Strong odor, slime or obvious deterioration are reasons to discard it before the second day.

What if it was previously frozen?

Thawed fish is still perishable. The product label and the timing of thawing matter. If you do not plan to cook it promptly, time the refrigerator thaw closer to when you will use it.

Freeze early rather than stretching the fridge window

If you buy fish Monday and already know you will not cook it until Thursday or Friday, freeze it Monday instead of holding it refrigerated for several days.

The practical takeaway

For fresh raw fish, think 1–2 days, not a week. Keep it at 40°F (4°C) or below and freeze it early if you do not expect to cook it within that window.

faq.question: Can I eat fresh fish after 3 days in the refrigerator?
faq.answer: USDA recommends only 1–2 refrigerated days for raw fish and shellfish before cooking or freezing, so three days is outside that guidance.

faq.question: What refrigerator temperature should fish be stored at?
faq.answer: 40°F (4°C) or below, with stable cold storage and protection from cross-contamination.

faq.question: Should I freeze fish on the second day?
faq.answer: If you know you will not cook it within 1–2 days, freezing it earlier is preferable to stretching the refrigerator window.
